title: Cap. 6 Arg. 7: Remonstrants—saving efficacy hangs on not opposing, not on omnipotent force
pass_a_gloss: So the Remonstrants, in the Declaration of their opinion concerning the third article, Acts of the Synod of Dordrecht, page 15. They say that the saving efficacy of grace depends neither on the congruity of the calling (as certain Papists) nor on the omnipotent divine force (as Prosper, Carmen De Ingratis, chapters 14 and 15, and Augustine, Against Julian, book 5, chapter 3; On the Predestination of the Saints, chapter 2; On Grace and Free Choice, chapter 20; and On Rebuke and Grace, chapter 14), but on such an operation as most certainly obtains its effect when the human being does not oppose rebellion, which from himself he could have opposed.
pass_b_english: So the Remonstrants put it in the Declaration of their view on the third article (Acts of the Synod of Dordrecht, p. 15). Saving efficacy of grace, they say, hangs neither on the fitness of the calling (as some Roman writers hold) nor on omnipotent divine force (as Prosper in the Carmen De Ingratis 14-15, and Augustine Against Julian 5.3, On the Predestination of the Saints 2, On Grace and Free Choice 20, and On Rebuke and Grace 14), but on an operation that most surely gets its effect when a person does not set rebellion against it—rebellion he could of himself have set.
source_text: Sic Remonstrantes, in Declaratione sententiae suae circa articulum tertium, Act. Synod. Dordrecht. pag. 15. Gratiae efficacitatem salutiferam pendere dicunt neque a congruitate vocationis (ut quidam Pontificii) neque ab omnipotente vi Divina, (ut Prosper, Carm. De Ingr. cap. 14. & 15. & Augustinus, Contra Julian. lib. 5. cap. 3. De praed. Sanct. cap. 2. De grat. & lib. arbit. cap. 20. & De corrept. & grat. cap. 14.) sed a tali operatione quae suum effectum certissime sortitur, cum rebellionem homo non opponit, quam ex se opponere potuisset.
